sources.concept: attacker-controlled WebAssembly module with an untaken conditional branch

impact.affected_asset: Integrity and confidentiality of the challenge V8 process; the injected print_flag executes cat /flag in this challenge environment.
impact.attacker_capability: Submit a crafted Wasm module whose control-flow and stack/register pressure trigger the untaken br_if tier-up path, then arrange a forged instance for call_indirect.
impact.security_effect: In the supplied CTF build, uninitialized stack disclosure and attacker-influenced fake-instance use can be escalated to program-counter control, reaching an injected flag-printing function.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled Wasm module contains a loop whose br_if condition is false, so the conditional branch's tier-up-check machine instructions are not executed at runtime.

The regression acquires an unused general-purpose register and uses LOAD_INSTANCE_FIELD despite nearby guidance not to modify CacheState or cache the instance; compilation records spills and a cached instance for conditionally emitted code that may not execute.

Later generated code trusts the stale CacheState: a value recorded as spilled is read from uninitialized machine-stack memory, and later instance accesses can consume an uninitialized register as the cached Wasm-instance pointer.

The documented challenge chain prepares controlled spilled values, supplies a fake Wasm instance, and uses call_indirect to obtain program-counter control and reach the challenge-injected print_flag function.

failure.operation: Subsequent Liftoff-generated spill reload and Wasm-instance access based on stale CacheState

primary_invariant.kind: compiler abstract-state / runtime-machine-state coherence across conditional emission
primary_invariant.statement: After a conditional control-flow path, Liftoff CacheState must describe only register and machine-stack state established on every feasible runtime path, or must be restored before subsequent code relies on it.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The patched br_if tier-up emission can update cache bookkeeping through temporary-register acquisition and instance caching even when its emitted code is skipped because the branch is not taken.

raw_refs.role: vulnerable regression patch and challenge sink

quality.review_notes: The organizer writeup, vulnerable patch, pinned build recipe, public trigger, and flag-delimiter healthcheck provide strong mechanism and oracle-contract evidence. The harness source establishes expected behavior but contains no recorded execution result. This is a deliberately reintroduced, build-specific CTF regression with an injected print_flag sink; no independently sourced upstream fix or production-version applicability is supplied. harness_fit is none_known because the available enum set has no TCP challenge-protocol harness category.

remediation.invariant_restored: CacheState agrees with the register and stack state actually established after both taken and untaken outcomes of the conditional path.
mitigation_classes: preserve or restore abstract compiler state at conditional control-flow joins
avoid cache-state-mutating temporary register allocation in conditionally skipped tier-up emission
avoid caching the Wasm instance in this emission path

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The public trigger supplies stack/register pressure and an untaken loop br_if; the documented escalation arranges controlled spilled values and a fake Wasm instance.
data_structure_invariants: Each CacheState register or spill-location claim must correspond to machine state that exists on the active runtime path.
The cached Wasm-instance register may be used only when that register was actually initialized with the instance on the active path.
state_context.state_machine: Liftoff translates Wasm stack values into machine registers or spill slots while CacheState tracks their abstract locations; a br_if can conditionally execute the tier-up-check code.
